newsitem.title: FINLAND: Construction bolsters Helsinki, weakness overseas.
newsitem.headline: Construction bolsters Helsinki, weakness overseas.

text.p: Finnish shares fell in thin trade on their first 1997 session on Thursday, but held up relatively well against declines in other European markets and Wall Street amid fears of higher U.S. interest rates, brokers said.
The HEX index slipped 0.51 percent to 2483.28, off earlier lows, with volume for the first session of the year a scant 285 million markka.

Stronger-than-expected U.S. economic data on Tuesday spoiled international sentiment but brokers here still hoped for a firm January and construction stocks took heart as Lemminkainen said it would make better-than expected 1996 profits.

Lemminkainen surged 4.40 markka or over 11 percent to 44.00 in healthy volume after upping its 1996 profit estimate to over 70 million markka. Its rivals Polar and YIT-Yhtyma followed with less dramatic gains in more modest dealings.
Many investors were still on the sidelines or extending their holidays, brokers said. "Some big investors haven't opened their books for the year yet," said one.
"Generally January is a good month for the bourse with buyers particularly active early in the year," said another.
Bourse engine Nokia traded below its New York close and closed thin 69 million markka trade 2.80 markka lower at 264.00.
Pharmaceuticals group Orion pared recent gains in line with Swedish drug giant Astra, in volumes active at over 30 million markka. Orion's more liquid B share ended 0.50 down at 176.50.
